proposal.title: End-to-end AWS sensor anomaly detection sketch
proposal.body: Scope: ingestion (IoT Core), durable buffering (Kinesis Data Streams), validation and scoring (Lambda), inference (SageMaker endpoint), quarantine for invalid events (SQS), results (DynamoDB) and operator alert (SNS). Assumptions: synthetic devices are existing callers outside provisioning; region and account are not selected; model type and labels are open. None of these paths has native generator coverage yet, so each remains an engineering gap. This is not a deployment.

data.label: Synthetic sensor devices
data.description: Existing synthetic event generator. Each event carries device_id, timestamp and value+unit. Outside provisioning scope.

data.label: Ingestion
data.description: Authenticates devices over MQTT and routes events via an IoT rule into Kinesis. Device certificates/policies need design.

data.label: Durable buffer
data.description: Durable, ordered buffer partitioned by device_id so events can be replayed. Retention period to be decided.

data.label: Validation & scoring
data.description: Consumes Kinesis batches; validates schema, device_id, timestamp and unit without altering them; sends invalid events to quarantine; calls the model; writes results idempotently keyed by device_id+timestamp; publishes alerts above threshold. Owns its role and logs.

data.label: Invalid event quarantine
data.description: Holds events that fail validation or processing, with the reason, for review and replay.

data.label: Anomaly model
data.description: Returns an anomaly score per event. Local tests use a scripted response; real accuracy needs a trained model and labelled evaluation.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: Stores device_id, timestamp, original value+unit, score, model version and decision.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Publishes anomaly alerts with device_id, timestamp and score. Subscription channel to be decided.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Person who receives and acts on anomaly alerts.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If identity, time or units are lost, operators can't trace or trust an anomaly.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."
requirementDrafts.statement: Every stored result and alert must keep the original device_id, event timestamp and value with its unit unchanged.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Proposed: prevents bad data from causing false alarms while keeping it for replay.
requirementDrafts.basis: User requested validation and durable buffering.
requirementDrafts.statement: Events that fail validation are kept with a reason in a quarantine queue and are never scored or silently dropped.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Too many false alarms make operators ignore alerts; too few miss failures.
requirementDrafts.statement: An operator is notified when an event's anomaly score crosses the agreed threshold; the threshold and false-alarm tolerance are still open.

response.message:
Where things stand: emulation ran 0 checks and stopped early, so nothing has been tested and the design isn't validated yet. The empty failures list doesn't mean the design is sound. The first blocker is the Ingestion step (AWS IoT Core → Kinesis), and no other block can be checked until it's built. That's because none of our blocks match a contract the export tool knows how to generate yet: IoT Core, Kinesis, the Kinesis-triggered Lambda scorer, the SageMaker endpoint, the SQS quarantine and SNS alerts all need product engineering work, and changing the drawing can't fix that. The reproducer for that work is this revision-2 artifact (digest b2f9847c…). I don't recommend switching to the S3/SQS word-count pipeline just to get a green check, because it counts words in documents and doesn't score sensor events. Doing that would quietly shrink our scope, so I've kept the diagram and requirements as they are.

The most useful thing we can decide now: for the first version, should the anomaly model be a simple fixed threshold per device and unit (for example, "temperature above 80 °C"), or a trained model? A threshold could live inside the scorer Lambda, which removes the SageMaker endpoint and its hourly cost from the first test. It also gives REQ-005 (the operator alert) a clear trigger to agree on. A trained model needs labelled anomalies before we can show it works.
